name: Somoy Countdown for Elementor
author: Md Rakib Miah

sections.description:
I built this because most countdown addons either come bundled inside a huge “all-in-one” widget pack or don’t give you enough control over how the boxes actually look. Somoy Countdown is just the one thing: drop it into Elementor, pick a target date, and style it however you want.

You get three layouts to start with — a simple List (the classic row of boxes), a Grid you can lock to 2, 3, or 4 columns, and a Circle style for rounder, badge-like timers. From there, everything is adjustable from Elementor’s own Style tab: background, padding, border, corner radius, shadow, number and label typography, colors, spacing — all of it. And since every size and spacing control is responsive, you can set one look for desktop and a tighter one for mobile without touching CSS.

What it does:

  • List, Grid, and Circle countdown layouts
  • Date & time picker for the target
  • Days / Hours / Minutes / Seconds boxes
  • Custom message once the countdown hits zero
  • Grid columns control (2, 3, or 4)
  • Full box styling — background, padding, border, radius, box-shadow
  • Separate color, typography, and spacing controls for the numbers and the labels
  • Independent desktop / tablet / mobile values on every layout and spacing control
  • Translation-ready
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip through WordPress admin → Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate it (you’ll need Elementor active too).
  3. Open the Elementor editor and search for “Somoy Countdown” in the widget panel — drag it onto the page.
  4. Pick a layout (List, Grid, or Circle) from the Content tab, then head to the Style tab to make it your own.
sections.faq:
Does this work without Elementor?

No — it’s built as an Elementor widget, so Elementor needs to be active on the site.

Can I use a different design on mobile than on desktop?

Yes. Gap, box size, padding, border radius, alignment, and grid columns all have the responsive (desktop/tablet/mobile) icon next to them, so you can set each breakpoint separately.

Will the countdown box shape change if I switch layouts later?

Yes, switching between List, Grid, and Circle updates the box shape immediately — you’ll just want to double check spacing and sizing afterward since each layout has its own defaults.

  • Added full box styling — padding, border, radius, box-shadow.
  • Added responsive controls for gap, box size, alignment, and grid columns.
  • Added a text-transform option for labels.
  • Renamed CSS classes to a unique rkcw- prefix to avoid conflicts with other plugins.
